securityDecisions: The email argument is an ownership claim, never a selector: it must equal the authenticated principal's normalized email, so the mutation cannot deactivate another account.
Deactivation revokes every session family in the same transaction as the SUSPENDED status change, so HTTP and WebSocket sessions both die.
Reactivation is only reachable by an already-active principal, because a suspended principal cannot authenticate; self-service recovery is therefore impossible by construction.

Identity resolution accepts only the CUSTOMER and RIDER applications that own this root, and only AUTHENTICATION_FAILED falls through to the next candidate — an infrastructure failure is never disguised as another application's rejection.

commands.command: pnpm --filter @fairbite/api exec vitest run --config vitest.config.ts test/unit/identity/deactivate.spec.ts
commands.detail: 2 tests: the ownership claim and requested state are forwarded; a rejection is propagated without inventing a result.

6 tests: exact app and web documents; SUSPENDED plus every session revoked; DEACTIVATE audit row; another account by email refused with both accounts unchanged; rider application principal served; reactivation keeps the session; non-boolean and anonymous callers rejected without side effects.

evidenceStatus.reason: The apps list is app, rider and web, so the evidence checker requires both web (W16) and device (W19) evidence. The record stays NOT_VERIFIED.

knownLimits: Latent defect found while implementing this root, outside its scope: the pre-existing refresh/logout/logoutAll revocations still pass a Node-side Date as revokedAt, which the same family CHECK can reject under container clock skew. They pass today, but they should move to the transaction clock like this root.
